chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-fuqqah (a type of bread), so he said, 'It is khamr (wine/intoxicant).'

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A type of bread, often associated with fermentation or specific preparation methods in classical texts.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: Wine or intoxicant; in this context, used to describe the nature or ruling of the bread.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of al-fuqqah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, 'Ammar ibn Musa asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the ruling of 'al-fuqqah' (a specific type of bread). The Imam replies that it is 'khamr' (wine/intoxicant), indicating that this particular bread was considered an intoxicant or had the ruling of wine, likely due to its fermentation or composition. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that substances causing intoxication, even in solid form, are classified under the category of *khamr*, thereby inheriting its prohibitions and ritual impurity (*najis*) status.
